newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO CONTINUES ASIAN EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO CONTINUES ASIAN EXPANSION.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO is marching on with its Asian expansion through the bid by ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia (Holdings) Ltd for 49 percent of Asia Securities Trading Public Co Ltd , analysts said on Wednesday.
"Asia is one of the areas they want to expand in in coming years," ING Barings analyst Daan Worm said.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia, a unit of the Dutch bank, earlier launched an offer of 2.2 billion baht for 49 percent of Asia Securites Trading at a price of 35 baht per share.
Asia Securities is a Thai retail and institutional securities business with investment banking operations.
ABN AMRO has previously indicated it wants to earn 15 percent of its group profits from Asia by 2000, compared with less than 10 percent now.
Analysts said the Dutch bank had lagged its international rivals in this fast-growing region in the past.
Bart van der Feen of IRIS said the problem with expansion in Asia was the lack of takeover targets.
"If there's a candidate they're going for it," he said.
The Thai offer is worth only $84 million and, he said, further acquisitions in the region may also be small, leaving big takeovers to be made in the United States.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia said it held no shares in AST but the two companies had been co-operating since 1991.
It said ABN AMRO bank also enjoyed a good relationship with Bangkok Bank , which owns 9.1 percent of AST.
ABN AMRO's latest annual report and a recent prospectus for its planned New York listing shows the Dutch bank owns 60 percent of HG Asia, now known as ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia.
But an ABN AMRO spokesman said the stake was now 70 percent, without giving further details.
Hong Kong's Guoco Group owns the other 30 percent.
